text: We have a side car product called Snyk Advisor. Snyk Advisor, it's basically a service that developers use to search and find open source packages when they're considering integrating some within their software applications.
speaker: Ben Williams
context: Lenny asks Ben about the growth tactics and content loops that have worked well for Snyk beyond their GitHub pull request strategy. Ben explains one of their successful programmatic SEO strategies through a product called Snyk Advisor. This tool helps developers search and evaluate open source packages by providing comprehensive metadata including security information and maintenance activity. The strategy works as a growth loop because developers searching for packages on Google find Snyk's indexed pages in search results, learn about package security, and are then directed to sign up for Snyk's main security platform.
text_ko: 저희는 Snyk Advisor라는 사이드카 제품(sidecar product)이 있어요. Snyk Advisor는 기본적으로 개발자들이 자신의 소프트웨어 애플리케이션(software applications)에 통합할지 고민할 때 오픈 소스 패키지(open source packages)를 검색하고 찾아볼 수 있게 해주는 서비스(service)에요.
text_zh: 我们有个附带产品叫Snyk Advisor。Snyk Advisor基本上就是给开发者用的一个服务，他们在考虑把一些开源包集成到自己的软件应用里时，可以用它来搜索和查找。
text_es: Tenemos un producto complementario que se llama Snyk Advisor. Snyk Advisor es básicamente un servicio que usan los desarrolladores para buscar y encontrar paquetes de código abierto cuando están viendo cuál integrar en sus aplicaciones de software.
key_sentence: Snyk Advisor, it's basically a service that developers use to search and find open source packages
original_text: We have a side car product called Snyk Advisor. Snyk Advisor, it's basically a service that developers use to search and find open source packages when they're considering integrating some within their software applications. The unique thing about it is it indexes all of the package managers. It learns about those packages. It augments the data about them with a bunch of metadata, including of course Snyk security scans, but we also find out how actively maintained the software is on the source repo on GitHub or wherever.

text: At the time, the only buyers were security teams and dev first Security for the most part wasn't something that CISOs and ApSec leaders were driving.
speaker: Ben Williams
context: Lenny asks about Snyk's early monetization challenges when their self-serve model struggled to gain traction with larger companies. Ben explains that in the early days, Snyk was ahead of the curve with their developer-first security approach. The problem was that security decisions were still controlled by traditional security teams (CISOs and Application Security leaders) who weren't yet driving developer-first initiatives. Ben describes how Snyk needed to position itself as a change agent helping companies transform their DevSecOps practices, which required building relationships with security decision-makers rather than just focusing on developer adoption.
text_ko: 그때는 구매자가 거의 보안팀(security teams)뿐이었고, 개발 우선 보안(dev-first security)은 대체로 CISO들(CISOs)이나 애플리케이션 보안 리더들(ApSec leaders)이 주도하는 영역이 아니었어요.
text_zh: 当时，买我们产品的基本上只有安全团队和开发团队，安全这块儿主要还是开发驱动的，CISO和应用安全(ApSec)负责人还没怎么参与进来。
text_es: En ese momento, los únicos que compraban eran los equipos de seguridad y los desarrolladores. La seguridad no era algo que estuvieran impulsando los CISOs ni los líderes de ApSec (Application Security).
key_sentence: Security for the most part wasn't something that CISOs and ApSec leaders were driving.
original_text: At the time, the only buyers were security teams and dev first Security for the most part wasn't something that CISOs and ApSec leaders were driving. But if you look at Snyk through that lens of, as I mentioned, being a change agent, being a key piece of the transformational journey of our customers' DevSecOps journeys, you realize how important it was for us to start to build relationships with those security leaders.

text: The ideal state is that every growth team member has common vocabulary. They're comfortable with the growth process. They can work well with data and experimentation platform. They understand the data. They have the right skills and mindset.
speaker: Ben Williams
context: Lenny asks Ben for advice on building effective growth teams, particularly in B2B product-led sales environments. Ben is explaining the first pillar of building successful growth teams: people and process. He emphasizes that team members need to be properly equipped with both skills and knowledge to do their best work. Ben explains that everyone on the growth team should share a common vocabulary around growth concepts, be comfortable with data and experimentation, and have the right mindset for growth work, which often involves rapid iteration and being comfortable with imperfection.
text_ko: 이상적으로는 모든 그로스 팀원(growth team member)이 공통의 용어를 써요. 그로스 프로세스(growth process)에 익숙해서 데이터(data)와 실험 플랫폼(experimentation platform)을 능숙하게 다루고, 데이터를 잘 이해해요. 필요한 기술과 올바른 마인드셋(mindset)을 갖추고 있어요.
text_zh: 理想状态就是增长团队里每个人都说得上话，对增长这套流程很熟悉，能熟练使用数据和实验平台，看得懂数据分析，技能和思维方式都到位。
text_es: Lo ideal es que todos los del equipo de crecimiento manejen el mismo vocabulario. Que se sientan cómodos con todo el proceso de growth. Que sepan trabajar bien con datos y las plataformas de experimentación. Que entiendan realmente los números. Y que tengan las habilidades y la mentalidad correctas.
key_sentence: Every growth team member should have a common vocabulary to align and uplevel the teams.
original_text: The ideal state is that every growth team member has common vocabulary. They're comfortable with the growth process. They can work well with data and experimentation platform. They understand the data. They have the right skills and mindset. Education I think plays a big part here. So we're big fans of Reforge, but we've also developed a bunch of internal programs to align and uplevel the teams.

text: You're never going to have a shortage of ideas in a high performing growth team. So, knowing where to focus amidst that kind of sea of ideas is a really important role of the strategy.
speaker: Ben Williams
context: Ben is explaining the importance of having a clear growth strategy to guide team execution. He's discussing how successful growth teams generate many ideas, but the real challenge is knowing where to focus efforts. Ben advocates for using a loop-based model to document and understand growth mechanisms. This involves identifying both small-scale (micro) and large-scale (macro) growth loops, understanding how they connect, and creating a shared framework that helps teams prioritize where to invest their time and resources among numerous potential opportunities.
text_ko: 성과가 높은 그로스팀(growth team)에서는 아이디어가 부족할 일이 없어요. 그래서 그런 아이디어의 바다 속에서 어디에 집중해야 할지를 아는 게 전략(strategy)의 정말 중요한 역할이에요.
text_zh: 高效增长团队从来不缺想法，问题在于面对这么多想法时，知道该把精力放在哪里，这就是战略的重要作用。
text_es: En un equipo de crecimiento que funciona bien nunca te van a faltar ideas. Entonces, saber en qué enfocarte en medio de ese mar de ideas es precisamente para lo que sirve la estrategia.
key_sentence: knowing where to focus amidst that kind of sea of ideas is a really important role of the strategy.
original_text: You're never going to have a shortage of ideas in a high performing growth team. So, knowing where to focus amidst that kind of sea of ideas is a really important role of the strategy. Being able to identify the various micro and macro loops, how they're all connected, being able to document them in a qualitative model to communicate a shared understanding of how you grow, it's really powerful.

text: We track a metric that we call product-driven revenue, which basically accounts for all revenue in customers where we saw meaningful value-based activity in the product before there was any sales contact.
speaker: Ben Williams
context: Lenny asks about freemium strategy and how to balance what goes in free versus paid plans. Ben is explaining how Snyk thinks about their product-led growth strategy in conjunction with their sales-led motion. He describes a key metric they use called 'product-driven revenue' which measures revenue from customers who engaged meaningfully with the product before any sales interaction occurred. This metric helps them understand how effectively their product-led approach contributes to overall business growth, even when sales teams are involved in closing deals.
text_ko: 우리는 ‘제품 주도 매출(product-driven revenue)’이라고 부르는 지표를 추적해요. 이 지표는 기본적으로 영업 쪽에서 접촉하기 전에 제품 안에서 의미 있는 가치 기반 활동(value-based activity)이 관찰된 고객으로부터 발생한 모든 수익을 포함해요.
text_zh: 我们追踪一个指标，叫做产品驱动收入(product-driven revenue)，说白了就是那些客户在销售还没接触之前，就已经在产品里有了实质性的价值行为，这部分产生的所有收入。
text_es: Hacemos seguimiento de una métrica que llamamos ingresos impulsados por producto (product-driven revenue), que básicamente mide todos los ingresos de clientes donde vimos actividad real de valor en el producto antes de que hubiera cualquier contacto comercial.
key_sentence: we saw meaningful value-based activity in the product before there was any sales contact.
original_text: We track a metric that we call product-driven revenue, which basically accounts for all revenue in customers where we saw meaningful value-based activity in the product before there was any sales contact. And that really tells actually a super interesting story about the PLG efficiency of your company across all revenue channels, self-serve and sales-led.

text: Flow is just this incredibly important concept for developers and you want to strive to keep them in that flow for as long as possible. The GitHub kind of pool requests are a great example of that.
speaker: Ben Williams
context: Lenny asks Ben about lessons for companies targeting developers and how to win their hearts and minds. Ben is explaining that the key to developer adoption is meeting developers where they already work rather than pulling them out of their existing workflows. He uses the concept of 'flow state' - when developers are deeply focused and productive - and explains how Snyk's GitHub integration allows developers to benefit from security improvements without disrupting their normal coding workflow. This approach allows one Snyk user to generate value for entire development teams without requiring everyone to sign up.
text_ko: 플로우(flow)는 개발자들에게 정말 중요한 개념이라서, 가능한 한 오래 그 상태를 유지시키려고 노력해야 해요. GitHub의 풀 리퀘스트(pull requests) 같은 방식이 그런 좋은 예예요.
text_zh: 心流(flow)对开发者来说真的太重要了，你得想办法让他们尽可能长时间地保持在那种状态里。GitHub的拉取请求(pull requests)就是个很好的例子。
text_es: El flujo de trabajo (flow) es un concepto súper importante para los desarrolladores y lo que buscas es mantenerlos en ese estado el mayor tiempo posible. Las solicitudes de extracción (pull requests) de GitHub son un ejemplo perfecto de eso.
key_sentence: you want to strive to keep them in that flow for as long as possible.
original_text: Flow is just this incredibly important concept for developers and you want to strive to keep them in that flow for as long as possible. The GitHub kind of pool requests are a great example of that. Someone can sign up for Snyk and they could theoretically be the only user of Snyk and connect their repos. All of a sudden we're protecting, securing those repos, a hundred, a thousand developers could be working in GitHub with that code, all benefiting from Snyk without necessarily needing to sign up.
